a: Integrated development environment
Internal data execution
Instruction design engine
Internet debugging extension
tasks.fb: An IDE combines programming facilities into one environment.

tasks.q: Match the core facility to its role.
pairs: Provide facilities needed to execute the program
tasks.fb: OCR J277 asks you to know these facilities and how they help program development.

tasks.q: Which facility lets a developer change price + quantity to price * quantity?
a: The source editor
The screen brightness control
The output window alone
A backup archive
tasks.fb: The editor changes source. The program must be rerun to test the change.

a: It supports a consistent layout and can reduce indentation mistakes
It guarantees the correct algorithm
It replaces the need to run tests
It permanently removes every syntax error
tasks.fb: Editor assistance reduces some effort, but the programmer must still check the result.

tasks.q: Which problem is most likely to produce a syntax diagnostic?
a: A missing closing bracket in a function call
A valid multiplication when addition was intended
A correct result printed in a small font
A variable with a meaningful name
tasks.fb: Syntax diagnostics concern the language rules. Valid syntax can still implement the wrong logic.

tasks.q: No syntax problems are reported, but the total is wrong. What should you inspect?
a: The calculation and the values it uses
Only the colour theme
Only the file icon
Nothing, because the result must be correct
tasks.fb: A logic error often requires tracing and testing rather than a syntax fix.

tasks.q: Which is the best test for a total price calculation?
a: Known price and quantity with an independently calculated expected total
Any data without an expected output
Changing the font and assuming success
Only opening the source file
tasks.fb: A test needs an expected result to compare with the actual output.

tasks.q: Why can a program fail during execution even after translation succeeds?
a: Some errors depend on the values or situation at runtime
Translation always prevents runtime problems
The editor must be closed first
Machine code never uses data
tasks.fb: For example, division by zero can depend on an input value. Successful translation alone is insufficient.

tasks.q: Set the breakpoint, inspect the values, repair the total calculation and pass both tests.
What does a variable watch help a developer do?
a: Inspect current values while debugging
Guarantee that every variable has the intended value
Turn source code into a photograph
Replace the specification
tasks.fb: The watch makes state visible. The programmer still decides whether those values are appropriate.

tasks.q: Choose the facility that directly addresses each need.
items: Read an explanation of a syntax problem
Execute the program and observe its output
Convert or process the source for execution
tasks.fb: Several facilities can work together when you press Run, but their roles are different.

tasks.q: After changing total = price + quantity to multiplication, what is the best next step?
a: Rerun tests with expected results for different inputs
Stop because any edit must be an improvement
Delete the output evidence
Change the variable names only
tasks.fb: Test the corrected source, including relevant cases that could reveal a remaining mistake.

tasks.q: A teacher wants evidence that an IDE helped locate a logic error. Which evidence is strongest?
a: A breakpoint and variable values showing where the wrong total was calculated
A screenshot of a new colour theme
The fact that no error message appeared
A larger font in the editor
tasks.fb: Useful debugging evidence connects a tool to the observed problem.

tasks.q: Match the action to the tool.
tasks.fb: These debugging facilities support investigation. Their names and layouts vary between IDEs.

info.title: One environment
info.text: An IDE brings tools for writing, translating, running and debugging code into one working environment. The exact features vary between products and languages. An IDE helps the programmer work; it does not choose the correct algorithm for them. Think: How could integration reduce the effort of checking a small change?

info.title: The source editor
info.text: The editor lets you write and change source code. Syntax highlighting can make keywords, strings and comments easier to distinguish. Auto-indentation or completion can reduce routine typing, but suggestions still need checking. Think: Why does syntax highlighting not prove that a calculation is correct?

info.title: Read the diagnostic
info.text: A syntax diagnostic can identify a location and describe invalid source. The reported location may be near the cause rather than the exact fix. A logic error can produce an incorrect result without a translation diagnostic. Think: A diagnostic says “unexpected closing bracket”. What should you do next?

info.title: Run and observe
info.text: The run-time environment supports execution and interaction with input and output. A translator may be invoked by a build or run command. Use expected results to decide whether the observed output is correct. Think: A ticket costs 4 and a customer buys 3. What output should a correct total calculation produce?

info.title: Pause and inspect
info.text: A breakpoint pauses execution at a chosen point. A variable watch shows values at that pause; stepping advances through instructions. Use the first unexpected value to narrow down the location of a logic error. Think: Where would you pause to inspect the inputs to a wrong total calculation?

info.title: Test the change
info.text: Fixing one example is not enough evidence for every input. Rerun relevant tests after changing source. Record the input, expected output, actual output and whether the test passed. Think: Why does testing two different orders provide stronger evidence than repeatedly testing the same order?
